data.body: [medium] Predictable shared temporary paths permit symlink-following writes. Lines 987-992 derive a global temporary directory from predictable process and thread identifiers. create_dir_all accepts a pre-existing attacker-controlled directory. Lines 997-1006 then write through attacker-provided golden.txt or evidence.json symlinks. A same-host user can overwrite any file writable by the test runner during normal test execution. Use a securely created private TempDir, or a private CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR path with exclusive file creation. Failure modes: arbitrary writable-file clobber and configuration or credential corruption. Edge cases: PID reuse, parallel runs, pre-created directories, and symlinked child files. Rollback: remove this self-test or replace its scratch allocator, then delete residual phase-b-del-03-bless-selftest directories. Monitoring: reject pre-existing roots and non-regular files. Record the private scratch root on failure. Validation: pre-create a symlink victim, run the test, and prove refusal leaves the victim unchanged. Also run concurrent instances.

[medium] The retained evidence count is false. This line claims 24 predicates, but phase-b-del-03.json contains 23 predicate objects. Its artifact predicate_count values also total 23. The generated PLAN_REQUIREMENTS summary repeats 24 while marking PHASE-B-DEL-03 satisfied. Correct the count to 23 or add the missing predicate, then regenerate. Failure modes: reviewers and automation accept an overstated evidence set. Edge cases: verdict remains met because no declared count is machine-checked. Rollback: restore active status or revert the delivered annotation until evidence agrees. Monitoring: emit a declared predicate_count from the renderer and compare it with the array length and artifact total. Validation: parse the committed JSON and assert declared count equals predicates length and grouped totals.

data.reason: Unresolved medium security finding: predictable shared temporary paths allow symlink-following file overwrite. Retained evidence also overstates 23 predicates as 24.

data.body: Fixed at 40bc7038-next. Root cause matched exactly: std::env::temp_dir() (world-writable /tmp on this host, 1777 root:root) joined with a predictable pid+thread name, created with create_dir_all (accepts a pre-existing attacker directory), then written through with std::fs::write (follows an existing symlink and truncates through it). Fix: (1) a new private_scratch_dir() helper allocates under env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR") (this crate's own target/tmp, 755 bob:bob -- not world-writable, confirmed by stat), names the candidate with pid+thread-id+a nanosecond timestamp+a retry counter, and creates it with std::fs::create_dir (not create_dir_all): that call fails outright on ANY pre-existing entry at the path -- file, directory, or symlink -- so a same-host attacker's pre-planted directory is refused rather than reused, and the loop retries a new name rather than falling back to accepting one. (2) bless() no longer calls std::fs::write directly; it goes through a new write_no_symlink() that opens with OpenOptions::create_new(true) first (O_CREAT|O_EXCL / CREATE_NEW -- atomic, no window for a planted symlink to be followed when nothing existed at the path yet, which is true for every self-test scratch file). The one legitimate case where something already exists -- PHASE_B_DEL_03_BLESS re-overwriting the already-committed golden/JSON -- falls back to symlink_metadata (does not follow) to confirm the existing entry is an ordinary regular file before overwriting; a symlink there is refused with an error instead of followed. Validation, exactly as asked: a new test, bless_refuses_to_follow_a_planted_symlink_rather_than_writing_through_it, creates a victim.txt with known content, symlinks golden.txt -> victim.txt, calls bless() at that path, and asserts victim.txt is byte-for-byte unchanged and golden_path is still a symlink (not replaced by a regular file). Both the pre-existing bless_always_panics... self-test and the new symlink self-test were re-run to green using private_scratch_dir/write_no_symlink; no leftover scratch dirs after either (remove_dir_all at the end of each). No new crates.io dependency: pure std (OpenOptions, symlink_metadata, env!(CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR)); tempfile is not a dev-dependency of continuum-asupersync and was not added.

Confirmed and fixed. The committed phase-b-del-03.json always had exactly 23 predicate objects (4+4+4+4+2+2+1+1+1 across the 9 artifacts, summed and verified with python3); the '24' was only ever in my own prose (plan.md's delivered annotation and my bone comment/report), never in the machine-checked JSON itself -- a human counting error on my part, now corrected in plan.md's annotation to '23'. Fixed as asked: (1) render_json now writes an explicit top-level "predicate_count":<preds.len()> field (previously the count was only implicit in the predicates array's own length), and render_golden gets a matching 'predicate count: N' line, both computed fresh from the live predicate list on every render, never hand-typed. (2) A new test, bnd_03_the_declared_predicate_count_matches_the_predicates_array_and_the_grouped_totals, parses the rendered JSON back out (no serde_json dependency -- the same light hand-rolled reading this file already used for PR15_JSON) and asserts: the number of rendered predicate objects (count of "pass": occurrences) equals preds.len(); the declared top-level predicate_count equals preds.len(); and the sum of every artifact's own predicate_count equals the declared total. (3) required() -- which aggregate() checks preds against -- was a self-referential predicates().iter().map(...) call, so it could never actually catch a whole predicate or predicate-generating function silently disappearing (both sides would shrink together and still report met). Replaced it with a hand-typed const REQUIRED: [(&str,&str); 23] static list (mirrors pr16_exit_evidence.rs's required(), 'derived from the static tables, not the results') naming the exact 23 (artifact,id) pairs; aggregate() is now a real pin -- bnd_01 already exercised flip/delete/duplicate/extra against it and still passes, now against a truly independent set. just fmt/clippy -D warnings clean; the file's own 15 tests (now including bnd_03 and the symlink test) pass; golden/JSON reblessed deliberately (PHASE_B_DEL_03_BLESS=1) with the diff reviewed -- one added 'predicate count: 23' line in the golden, one field added to the JSON, nothing else moved.

[resolved] The target closes the medium overwrite finding. private_scratch_dir creates an unpredictable child with create_dir under the crate target tmp directory. Fresh outputs use create_new, and existing final-path symlinks are refused. Failure modes: pre-planted scratch entries and final-path symlinks now fail closed. Edge cases: name collisions retry, dangling symlinks are refused, and repeat blessing accepts only a regular existing entry. Rollback: revert the delivery annotation or disable PHASE_B_DEL_03_BLESS if this writer regresses. Monitoring: retain byte-stability failures and surface path errors. Validation: inspected the exclusive-create and planted-symlink paths at b7202fa; tests were not rerun in this metadata-only review.

[resolved] The target closes the count finding. REQUIRED independently pins all 23 pairs. The JSON and golden counts derive from preds.len(), and the parsed committed JSON has 23 objects and grouped total 23. Failure modes: missing, duplicate, extra, failing, or count-drifted predicates produce not-met or fail the stability test. Edge cases: a whole predicate producer cannot shrink the independent required set. Rollback: restore PHASE-B-DEL-03 to active if counts diverge. Monitoring: compare declared, array, and grouped totals. Validation: parsed the committed JSON and inspected bnd_01 and bnd_03; tests were not rerun in this metadata-only review.
